lines.text: Doctors told this kid's parents he might never grow.
He was eleven, and smaller than every boy on the field.
His body wasn't making enough growth hormone.
The treatment cost almost a thousand dollars a month.
His dad worked in a steel factory.
They couldn't afford it.
So every night, this kid pushed a needle into his own legs.
Every. Single. Night.
His club stopped paying, and the big clubs wouldn't take the risk.
Then, at thirteen, he crossed an ocean for one tryout in Spain.
The coaches watched him play, and they didn't want to wait for paperwork.
So they signed him on a paper napkin.
At seventeen, he was playing for one of the biggest clubs in the world.
Then came the heartbreak.
He lost a World Cup final.
Then two more finals for his country.
Three years in a row.
He quit the national team.
But he came back.
And at thirty-five, he finally lifted the World Cup.
Eight Ballon d'Ors. More than anyone in history.
That kid who might never grow?
His name is Lionel Messi.
And he still stands just five foot seven.
